# Welcome

This is an optional step after the analysis for the paper *"Knowledge Gaps and Sequencing Priorities for Mammalian eDNA Metabarcoding in the World's Largest Tropical Forest Country"*. It does not change any result in the paper.

It writes the data for the interactive website in `docs/` (served with GitHub Pages): the priority list of all 731 species, the species in each 25 × 25 km grid cell, the map outlines, and the reference sequences of Brazilian mammals per primer. The website itself (`docs/index.html` and `docs/assets/`) is static and does not need to be rebuilt; this document only replaces the files in `docs/data/`.

**Inputs:** `output/intermediate/1_Prepare_data.rds` (Part 1), `output/intermediate/2_Assess_completeness_ambiguity_complementarity.rds` (Part 2), `output/intermediate/4_Barcoding_priorities.rds` (Part 4), and the cached range polygons and biome borders from Part 4.

**Output:** `docs/data/`.

## Maintaining the website

**Files.** The site is a static page in `docs/`, served with GitHub Pages (repository Settings \> Pages: deploy from the `main` branch, folder `/docs`).

- `docs/index.html`, `docs/assets/css/site.css`, `docs/assets/js/site.js`: page, styles and behaviour.
- `docs/assets/js/i18n.js`: all interface text, in English (`en`) and Portuguese (`pt`). Edit the text there. Keys must exist in both languages.
- `docs/assets/vendor/`, `docs/assets/fonts/`, `docs/assets/img/`: Leaflet, Tabulator, the fonts (Spectral, IBM Plex Sans Condensed, SIL Open Font Licence) and the placeholder image, all stored locally.
- `docs/data/`: written by this document (species table, priority species per grid cell, all species per grid cell as bit sets for the location filter, map outlines, rivers and cities, Wikipedia summaries, reference sequences, site information).
- `docs/img/species/`: species thumbnails, downloaded by this document.

**Settings** (chunk "Settings" below): Zenodo DOI, repository, article DOI (ADD THIS ONCE PUBLISHED).

**Corrections.** Wrong photos can be rectified with `photo_overrides`. Wrong or missing descriptions can be rectified with `summary_overrides`. Wrong common names can be rectified with `common_name_overrides`. If any of these are changedm the documents needs to be re-rendered and pushed.

**Online data are cached** in `output/cache/` (`website_links.rds`, `website_photos.rds`, `website_summaries.rds`, `website_summaries_pt.rds`). Delete a file, or set `rebuild_cache <- TRUE`, to query the online sources again.

**Updating the site.** Render this document, then commit and push `docs/` (for example with GitHub Desktop). GitHub Pages rebuilds the site. Reload it with Ctrl+Shift+R to bypass the browser cache. To preview locally, run `servr::httd("docs")`.

**Shareable links.** The address keeps the current view, e.g. `…/#lang=pt&cat=research&persp=local&sp=Cyclopes_rufus&cell=144_114`.

# 1. Species table

**Common names:**

Common names from the Mammal Diversity Database (`rmdd`), matched on accepted names and then synonyms, for all species. The manual names are the same as in Part 4.

```{r}

mdd_key  <- function(x) tolower(gsub("[_ ]+", " ", trimws(x)))
mdd      <- rmdd::mdd_checklist
accepted <- setNames(mdd$main_common_name, mdd_key(mdd$sci_name))

syn <- unique(data.frame(
  key      = mdd_key(rmdd::mdd_synonyms$mdd_original_combination),
  accepted = mdd_key(rmdd::mdd_synonyms$mdd_species)
))
syn <- syn[!is.na(syn$key) & syn$accepted %in% names(accepted), ]
syn <- syn[!syn$key %in% syn$key[duplicated(syn$key)], ]
synonym_names <- setNames(accepted[syn$accepted], syn$key)

keys <- mdd_key(brz_mam_taxonomy$binomial)
common_names <- unname(accepted[keys])
via_synonym <- is.na(common_names) & keys %in% names(synonym_names)
common_names[via_synonym] <- unname(synonym_names[keys[via_synonym]])
names(common_names) <- brz_mam_taxonomy$binomial

common_name_overrides <- c(
  "Aotus infulatus"          = "Feline Night Monkey",
  "Pithecia inusta"          = "Burnished Saki",
  "Alouatta puruensis"       = "Purus Red Howler",
  "Metachirus arinatai"      = "Aritana's Brown Four-eyed Opossum",
  "Rhipidomys cearanus"      = "Ceará Climbing Mouse",
  "Rhipidomys baturiteensis" = "Baturité Climbing Mouse",
  "Sylvilagus minensis"      = "Minas Gerais Tapeti",
  "Sylvilagus paraguensis"   = "Paraguayan Tapeti",
  "Makalata obscura"         = "Dusky Spiny Tree-rat"
)
common_names[names(common_name_overrides)] <- common_name_overrides

message(sum(is.na(common_names)), " species without a common name")

rm(mdd_key, mdd, accepted, syn, synonym_names, keys, via_synonym, common_name_overrides)

```

**Links to Wikipedia and GBIF:**

English Wikipedia pages are found through Wikidata (taxon name, property P225), and GBIF species pages through the GBIF backbone taxonomy. Both are online queries, so the results are cached. Species without a Wikipedia page get no link.

```{r}

if (needs_build("website_links.rds")) {

  # 1. Wikipedia: query Wikidata in batches of 100 names

  query_wikipedia <- function(names) {
    values <- paste0('"', names, '"', collapse = " ")
    query <- paste0(
      'SELECT ?name ?article WHERE { VALUES ?name { ', values, ' } ',
      '?item wdt:P225 ?name . ',
      '?article schema:about ?item ; schema:isPartOf <https://en.wikipedia.org/> . }'
    )
    res <- httr::GET("https://query.wikidata.org/sparql",
                     query = list(query = query, format = "json"),
                     httr::user_agent("Brazilian mammal sequencing priorities (research website)"),
                     httr::timeout(60))
    httr::stop_for_status(res)
    rows <- jsonlite::fromJSON(httr::content(res, as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8"))$results$bindings
    if (length(rows) == 0) return(data.frame(binomial = character(), wikipedia = character()))
    data.frame(binomial = rows$name$value, wikipedia = rows$article$value)
  }

  batches <- split(brz_mam_taxonomy$binomial, ceiling(seq_along(brz_mam_taxonomy$binomial) / 100))
  wikipedia <- bind_rows(lapply(batches, function(b) { Sys.sleep(1); query_wikipedia(b) })) %>%
    distinct(binomial, .keep_all = TRUE)

  # 2. GBIF: backbone key of each species

  gbif <- rgbif::name_backbone_checklist(brz_mam_taxonomy$binomial) %>%
    transmute(binomial = verbatim_name,
              gbif_key = ifelse(matchType %in% c("EXACT", "FUZZY") & rank == "SPECIES", usageKey, NA))

  links <- brz_mam_taxonomy %>%
    select(binomial) %>%
    left_join(wikipedia, by = "binomial") %>%
    left_join(gbif, by = "binomial")

  saveRDS(links, cache_file("website_links.rds"))

  rm(query_wikipedia, batches, wikipedia, gbif, links)
}

links <- readRDS(cache_file("website_links.rds"))

message(sum(!is.na(links$wikipedia)), " species with a Wikipedia page, ",
        sum(!is.na(links$gbif_key)), " with a GBIF key")

```

**Species photos:**

One photo per species, shown as a thumbnail in the website's priority list. Photos come from iNaturalist (the featured photo, or another of its photos if the featured one is not openly licensed) and, for species without one, from Wikimedia Commons (the Wikidata image of the taxon, property P18). Only openly licensed photos are used (CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA, CC BY-NC, CC BY-NC-SA, public domain), and each is credited on the website. Species without a photo get a placeholder. Both are online queries, so the results are cached.

Photos can be replaced or removed by hand in `photo_overrides` (for example a misidentified photo). Set `image_url` to `NA` to show the placeholder instead.

```{r}

photo_overrides <- tibble::tribble(
  ~binomial, ~image_url, ~credit, ~page
  # "Genus species", "https://…/photo.jpg", "(c) Name, CC BY", "https://…",
)

open_licences_inat <- c("cc0", "cc-by", "cc-by-sa", "cc-by-nc", "cc-by-nc-sa")
ua <- httr::user_agent("Brazilian mammal sequencing priorities (research website; https://github.com/ThomasLuypaert/brazil-mammal-edna-priorities)")

# GET a JSON API with retries

get_json <- function(url, query = list()) {
  for (attempt in 1:3) {
    res <- tryCatch(httr::GET(url, query = query, ua, httr::timeout(60)), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(res) && httr::status_code(res) == 200)
      return(jsonlite::fromJSON(httr::content(res, as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8"), simplifyVector = FALSE))
    Sys.sleep(if (!is.null(res) && httr::status_code(res) == 429) 60 else 5)
  }
  NULL
}

if (needs_build("website_photos.rds")) {

  # 1. iNaturalist: match the species name 

  inat_photo <- function(name) {
    Sys.sleep(1.1)   # iNaturalist asks for at most 60 requests per minute
    hits <- get_json("https://api.inaturalist.org/v1/taxa",
                     list(q = name, rank = "species", per_page = 10))$results
    is_match <- function(t) identical(t$iconic_taxon_name, "Mammalia") &&
      (tolower(t$name) == tolower(name) || tolower(t$matched_term %||% "") == tolower(name))
    taxon <- Find(is_match, hits)
    if (is.null(taxon)) return(NULL)

    is_open <- function(p) !is.null(p) && tolower(p$license_code %||% "") %in% open_licences_inat
    photo <- taxon$default_photo
    if (!is_open(photo)) {
      Sys.sleep(1.1)
      details <- get_json(paste0("https://api.inaturalist.org/v1/taxa/", taxon$id))$results
      photos  <- lapply(details[[1]]$taxon_photos %||% list(), `[[`, "photo")
      photo   <- Find(is_open, photos)
    }
    if (is.null(photo)) return(NULL)

    url <- photo$medium_url %||% photo$url
    data.frame(binomial  = name,
               source    = "iNaturalist",
               image_url = sub("/(square|thumb|medium|large|original)\\.", "/small.", url),
               credit    = photo$attribution %||% "iNaturalist",
               page      = paste0("https://www.inaturalist.org/photos/", photo$id))
  }

  names_all <- brz_mam_taxonomy$binomial
  inat <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(names_all), function(i) {
    if (i %% 50 == 0) message("iNaturalist: ", i, " of ", length(names_all))
    inat_photo(names_all[i])
  }))

  # 2. Wikimedia Commons, for species without an iNaturalist photo

  remaining <- setdiff(names_all, inat$binomial)

  wikidata_images <- function(names) {
    values <- paste0('"', names, '"', collapse = " ")
    query <- paste0('SELECT ?name ?image WHERE { VALUES ?name { ', values, ' } ',
                    '?item wdt:P225 ?name . ?item wdt:P18 ?image . }')
    rows <- get_json("https://query.wikidata.org/sparql", list(query = query, format = "json"))$results$bindings
    if (length(rows) == 0) return(data.frame(binomial = character(), file = character()))
    data.frame(binomial = vapply(rows, function(r) r$name$value, ""),
               file     = vapply(rows, function(r) URLdecode(sub(".*/Special:FilePath/", "", r$image$value)), ""))
  }

  commons_photo <- function(name, file) {
    Sys.sleep(0.5)
    info <- get_json("https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/api.php",
                     list(action = "query", titles = paste0("File:", file), prop = "imageinfo",
                          iiprop = "url|extmetadata", iiurlwidth = 240, format = "json"))
    ii <- info$query$pages[[1]]$imageinfo[[1]]
    if (is.null(ii)) return(NULL)
    licence <- ii$extmetadata$LicenseShortName$value %||% ""
    if (!grepl("^(CC0|CC BY|Public domain|PD)", licence, ignore.case = TRUE) || grepl("ND", licence)) return(NULL)
    artist <- trimws(gsub("\\s+", " ", gsub("<[^>]+>", "", ii$extmetadata$Artist$value %||% "Unknown author")))
    data.frame(binomial  = name,
               source    = "Wikimedia Commons",
               image_url = ii$thumburl %||% ii$url,
               credit    = paste0(substr(artist, 1, 80), ", ", licence, " (Wikimedia Commons)"),
               page      = ii$descriptionurl)
  }

  batches <- split(remaining, ceiling(seq_along(remaining) / 100))
  wd <- bind_rows(lapply(batches, function(b) { Sys.sleep(1); wikidata_images(b) })) %>%
    distinct(binomial, .keep_all = TRUE)
  commons <- bind_rows(Map(commons_photo, wd$binomial, wd$file))

  photos <- bind_rows(inat, commons)
  saveRDS(photos, cache_file("website_photos.rds"))

  rm(inat_photo, names_all, inat, remaining, wikidata_images, commons_photo, batches, wd, commons, photos)
}

photos <- readRDS(cache_file("website_photos.rds"))

# Manual corrections

photos <- photos %>%
  filter(!binomial %in% photo_overrides$binomial) %>%
  bind_rows(photo_overrides %>% filter(!is.na(image_url)) %>% mutate(source = "manual"))

message(nrow(photos), " species with a photo (",
        sum(photos$source == "iNaturalist"), " iNaturalist, ",
        sum(photos$source == "Wikimedia Commons"), " Wikimedia Commons, ",
        sum(photos$source == "manual"), " manual); ",
        nrow(brz_mam_taxonomy) - nrow(photos), " without")

rm(photo_overrides, open_licences_inat)

```

**Species summaries (English and Portuguese):**

A short description of each species with a Wikipedia page. The first sentences of the article's summary (Wikipedia page summary API), at most about 280 characters, shown in the website's species card with a link to the article. English summaries come from the English Wikipedia pages found above. Portuguese summaries from the Portuguese Wikipedia pages, found through Wikidata in the same way. The Portuguese version of the website falls back to the English summary where there is no Portuguese one. Wikipedia text is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 and attributed on the website. The results are cached.

Summaries can be replaced or removed by hand in `summary_overrides` (`lang` is `"en"` or `"pt"`). Set `text` to `NA` to remove one.

```{r}

summary_overrides <- tibble::tribble(
  ~binomial, ~lang, ~text
  # "Genus species", "en", "Replacement text.",
)

# Summary of one Wikipedia article (url: the article's address)

wiki_summary <- function(name, url) {
  Sys.sleep(0.2)
  domain <- sub("^(https?://[^/]+)/.*$", "\\1", url)
  title  <- sub(".*/wiki/", "", url)
  js <- get_json(paste0(domain, "/api/rest_v1/page/summary/", title))
  if (is.null(js) || !identical(js$type, "standard") || is.null(js$extract)) return(NULL)
  data.frame(binomial = name,
             extract  = js$extract,
             page     = js$content_urls$desktop$page %||% url)
}

# 1. English

if (needs_build("website_summaries.rds")) {
  with_page <- links %>% filter(!is.na(wikipedia))
  summaries_en <- bind_rows(Map(wiki_summary, with_page$binomial, with_page$wikipedia))
  saveRDS(summaries_en, cache_file("website_summaries.rds"))
  rm(with_page, summaries_en)
}

# 2. Portuguese: find the Portuguese Wikipedia pages through Wikidata (taxon name, P225)

if (needs_build("website_summaries_pt.rds")) {

  query_ptwiki <- function(names) {
    values <- paste0('"', names, '"', collapse = " ")
    query <- paste0(
      'SELECT ?name ?article WHERE { VALUES ?name { ', values, ' } ',
      '?item wdt:P225 ?name . ',
      '?article schema:about ?item ; schema:isPartOf <https://pt.wikipedia.org/> . }'
    )
    rows <- get_json("https://query.wikidata.org/sparql", list(query = query, format = "json"))$results$bindings
    if (length(rows) == 0) return(data.frame(binomial = character(), wikipedia_pt = character()))
    data.frame(binomial     = vapply(rows, function(r) r$name$value, ""),
               wikipedia_pt = vapply(rows, function(r) r$article$value, ""))
  }

  batches  <- split(brz_mam_taxonomy$binomial, ceiling(seq_along(brz_mam_taxonomy$binomial) / 100))
  links_pt <- bind_rows(lapply(batches, function(b) { Sys.sleep(1); query_ptwiki(b) })) %>%
    distinct(binomial, .keep_all = TRUE)
  summaries_pt <- bind_rows(Map(wiki_summary, links_pt$binomial, links_pt$wikipedia_pt))

  saveRDS(list(links = links_pt, summaries = summaries_pt), cache_file("website_summaries_pt.rds"))
  rm(query_ptwiki, batches, links_pt, summaries_pt)
}

# Keep whole sentences up to about 280 characters 

shorten <- function(x, max_chars = 280) {
  if (is.na(x) || !nzchar(trimws(x))) return(NA_character_)   # empty summaries
  x <- trimws(gsub("\\s+", " ", x))
  sentences <- trimws(regmatches(x, gregexpr(".+?(?:[.!?]+(?=\\s+[\\p{Lu}(])|$)", x, perl = TRUE))[[1]])
  sentences <- sentences[nzchar(sentences)]
  if (!length(sentences)) return(x)
  out <- sentences[1]
  for (s in sentences[-1]) {
    if (nchar(out) + 1 + nchar(s) > max_chars) break
    out <- paste(out, s)
  }
  if (nchar(out) > max_chars + 60) out <- paste0(sub("\\s+\\S*$", "", substr(out, 1, max_chars)), "…")
  out
}

pt_cache  <- readRDS(cache_file("website_summaries_pt.rds"))
links_pt  <- pt_cache$links

summaries <- bind_rows(
  readRDS(cache_file("website_summaries.rds")) %>% mutate(lang = "en"),
  pt_cache$summaries %>% mutate(lang = "pt")
) %>%
  mutate(text = vapply(extract, shorten, "")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(text)) %>%
  select(binomial, lang, text, page) %>%
  anti_join(summary_overrides, by = c("binomial", "lang")) %>%
  bind_rows(summary_overrides %>% filter(!is.na(text)) %>%
              left_join(bind_rows(links %>% transmute(binomial, lang = "en", page = wikipedia),
                                  links_pt %>% transmute(binomial, lang = "pt", page = wikipedia_pt)),
                        by = c("binomial", "lang")))

message(sum(summaries$lang == "en"), " species with an English and ",
        sum(summaries$lang == "pt"), " with a Portuguese Wikipedia summary")

rm(summary_overrides, shorten, wiki_summary, pt_cache)

```

**Build the species table:**

Species are numbered in alphabetical order, and the numbers link the species table to the grid cells and the sequences.

```{r}

primers_with_sequence <- brz_mam_completeness_all %>%
  group_by(binomial) %>%
  summarise(n_primers = sum(presence > 0), .groups = "drop")

site_species <- brz_mam_taxonomy %>%
  select(binomial, order, family) %>%
  arrange(binomial) %>%
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()) - 1L) %>%
  left_join(priority_species_flags %>% select(binomial, global_category, local_category), by = "binomial") %>%
  left_join(EDGE2_species %>% select(binomial, iucn_status, salve_status,
                                     median_BREDGE_global, median_BREDGE_brz,
                                     median_ED_global, median_ED_brz,
                                     median_pext_global, median_pext_brz,
                                     median_exclusion_prob_global), by = "binomial") %>%
  left_join(primers_with_sequence, by = "binomial") %>%
  left_join(links, by = "binomial") %>%
  left_join(links_pt, by = "binomial") %>%
  mutate(across(c(global_category, local_category), ~ replace_na(.x, "None")),
         n_primers = replace_na(n_primers, 0L),
         common_name = unname(common_names[binomial]),
         has_range_map = !binomial %in% species_without_range_map)

stopifnot(nrow(site_species) == nrow(brz_mam_taxonomy), !any(duplicated(site_species$binomial)))

species_id <- setNames(site_species$id, site_species$binomial)

# Thumbnails are stored with the website so the site does not depend on the photo sources being online

img_dir <- here("docs", "img", "species")
dir.create(img_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

download_photo <- function(url, id) {
  ext <- tolower(tools::file_ext(sub("\\?.*$", "", url)))
  if (!ext %in% c("jpg", "jpeg", "png", "webp")) ext <- "jpg"
  dest <- file.path(img_dir, paste0(id, ".", ext))
  if (!file.exists(dest)) {
    Sys.sleep(0.3)
    ok <- tryCatch(httr::status_code(httr::GET(url, ua, httr::timeout(60),
                                               httr::write_disk(dest, overwrite = TRUE))) == 200,
                   error = function(e) FALSE)
    if (!ok) { unlink(dest); return(NA_character_) }
  }
  paste0("img/species/", basename(dest))
}

photos <- photos %>%
  mutate(id = unname(species_id[binomial])) %>%
  filter(!is.na(id))
photos$image <- as.character(unlist(Map(download_photo, photos$image_url, photos$id)))

# Remove thumbnails of species that no longer have a photo

stale <- setdiff(list.files(img_dir), basename(na.omit(photos$image)))
unlink(file.path(img_dir, stale))

site_species <- site_species %>%
  left_join(photos %>% filter(!is.na(image)) %>% select(binomial, image, credit, page), by = "binomial")

message(sum(!is.na(site_species$image)), " thumbnails, ",
        round(sum(file.size(list.files(img_dir, full.names = TRUE))) / 1e6, 1), " MB")

# Short field names keep the file small; see docs/assets/js/site.js

species_json <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(site_species)), function(i) {
  s <- site_species[i, ]
  list(
    id = unbox(s$id), b = unbox(s$binomial), c = unbox(coalesce(s$common_name, "")),
    o = unbox(s$order), f = unbox(s$family),
    gc = unbox(s$global_category), lc = unbox(s$local_category),
    iu = unbox(s$iucn_status), sa = unbox(s$salve_status),
    bg = unbox(round(s$median_BREDGE_global, 3)), bl = unbox(round(s$median_BREDGE_brz, 3)),
    eg = unbox(round(s$median_ED_global, 2)), el = unbox(round(s$median_ED_brz, 2)),
    ge = unbox(round(s$median_pext_global, 3)), le = unbox(round(s$median_pext_brz, 3)),
    po = unbox(round(s$median_exclusion_prob_global, 3)),
    np = unbox(s$n_primers),
    w = unbox(if (is.na(s$wikipedia)) NA else s$wikipedia),
    wp = unbox(if (is.na(s$wikipedia_pt)) NA else s$wikipedia_pt),
    gb = unbox(if (is.na(s$gbif_key)) NA else as.integer(s$gbif_key)),
    rm = unbox(s$has_range_map),
    im = unbox(if (is.na(s$image)) NA else s$image),
    ic = unbox(if (is.na(s$image)) NA else s$credit),
    ip = unbox(if (is.na(s$image)) NA else s$page)
  )
})

write_json_compact(list(species = species_json), file.path(data_dir, "species.json"))

# Wikipedia summaries

summary_ids <- unique(summaries$binomial)
pick <- function(name, l, field) {
  x <- summaries[[field]][summaries$binomial == name & summaries$lang == l]
  if (length(x)) x[1] else NA
}
summaries_json <- setNames(
  lapply(summary_ids, function(b) c(pick(b, "en", "text"), pick(b, "en", "page"),
                                    pick(b, "pt", "text"), pick(b, "pt", "page"))),
  unname(species_id[summary_ids])
)
summaries_json <- summaries_json[!is.na(names(summaries_json))]
write_json_compact(summaries_json, file.path(data_dir, "summaries.json"))

rm(primers_with_sequence, species_json, common_names, links, photos, img_dir, download_photo, stale, get_json, ua,
   summaries, summaries_json, summary_ids, pick, links_pt)

```

# 2. Map data

**Grid cells and the priority species in each cell:**

The grid is built exactly as in Part 4 (25 × 25 km cells in EPSG:3857, anchored at the lower-left corner of Brazil's bounding box), so that the website can find the cell of any clicked point from its coordinates.

```{r}

brazil      <- ne_countries(country = "Brazil", scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf") %>% st_transform(4326)
brazil_proj <- st_transform(brazil, 3857)

resolution_m <- 25000
origin <- st_bbox(brazil_proj)

grid_sf_proj <- st_sf(geometry = st_make_grid(brazil_proj, cellsize = resolution_m, square = TRUE))
grid_sf_proj <- grid_sf_proj[st_intersects(grid_sf_proj, brazil_proj, sparse = FALSE), ]

range_polygons <- readRDS(cache_file("brazilian_range_polygons.rds"))
intersections  <- st_intersects(grid_sf_proj, range_polygons, sparse = TRUE)

# Column and row of each cell, counted from the grid origin

centres <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_geometry(grid_sf_proj)))
cell_col <- floor((centres[, 1] - origin[["xmin"]]) / resolution_m)
cell_row <- floor((centres[, 2] - origin[["ymin"]]) / resolution_m)

# Priority species (either perspective) in each cell, as species numbers

priority_ids <- species_id[site_species$binomial[site_species$global_category != "None" |
                                                 site_species$local_category  != "None"]]

cells <- lapply(intersections, function(i) {
  ids <- unname(species_id[unique(range_polygons$binomial[i])])
  sort(as.integer(intersect(ids, priority_ids)))
})
names(cells) <- paste0(cell_col, "_", cell_row)

stopifnot(!any(duplicated(names(cells))))

write_json_compact(
  list(crs  = unbox("EPSG:3857"),
       xmin = unbox(origin[["xmin"]]), ymin = unbox(origin[["ymin"]]),
       res  = unbox(resolution_m),
       ncol = unbox(as.integer(max(cell_col) + 1)), nrow = unbox(as.integer(max(cell_row) + 1)),
       cells = cells),
  file.path(data_dir, "grid.json")
)

message(length(cells), " grid cells; ", sum(lengths(cells) > 0), " with at least one priority species")

```

**All species in each cell:**

For the location filter of the sequence downloads, the website needs every species whose range overlaps a cell, not only the priority species. To keep the file small, each cell's species are stored as a bit set (one bit per species number, base64-encoded), and cells with the same species share one bit set.

```{r}

n_bits <- 8 * ceiling(nrow(site_species) / 8)

cell_sets <- vapply(intersections, function(i) {
  ids  <- unname(species_id[unique(range_polygons$binomial[i])])
  bits <- logical(n_bits)
  bits[ids[!is.na(ids)] + 1] <- TRUE
  jsonlite::base64_enc(packBits(bits, type = "raw"))   # bit k of byte j = species 8j + k
}, character(1))

unique_sets <- unique(cell_sets)
cell_index  <- setNames(as.list(match(cell_sets, unique_sets) - 1L), names(cells))

write_json_compact(
  list(n_species = unbox(nrow(site_species)),
       sets      = unique_sets,
       cells     = lapply(cell_index, unbox)),
  file.path(data_dir, "grid_all.json")
)

message(length(unique_sets), " distinct species sets across ", length(cell_sets), " cells")

rm(grid_sf_proj, range_polygons, intersections, centres, cell_col, cell_row, priority_ids, cells, origin,
   n_bits, cell_sets, unique_sets, cell_index)

```

**Outlines of Brazil and its biomes, major rivers and reference cities:**

Simplified for the web, with coordinates rounded to about 10 m.

```{r}

write_geojson <- function(x, file) {
  if (file.exists(file)) file.remove(file)
  st_write(x, file, driver = "GeoJSON", quiet = TRUE,
           layer_options = c("COORDINATE_PRECISION=4", "RFC7946=YES"))
}

brazil_simple <- brazil %>%
  st_transform(5880) %>%
  st_simplify(dTolerance = 1000) %>%
  st_transform(4326) %>%
  transmute(name = "Brazil")

write_geojson(brazil_simple, file.path(data_dir, "brazil.geojson"))

biome_names <- c("Amazonia" = "Amazon", "Mata Atlantica" = "Atlantic Forest", "Caatinga" = "Caatinga",
                 "Cerrado" = "Cerrado", "Pampa" = "Pampa", "Pantanal" = "Pantanal")

biomes_simple <- readRDS(cache_file("biomes.rds")) %>%
  mutate(name_ascii = iconv(name_biome, to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT")) %>%
  filter(name_ascii %in% names(biome_names)) %>%
  transmute(biome = unname(biome_names[name_ascii])) %>%
  st_make_valid() %>%
  st_transform(5880) %>%
  st_simplify(preserveTopology = TRUE, dTolerance = 2000) %>%
  st_transform(4326)

write_geojson(biomes_simple, file.path(data_dir, "biomes.geojson"))

# Major rivers and reference cities, as in Fig. 5 (cached in Part 4)

ne_layers <- readRDS(cache_file("natural_earth_layers.rds"))

rivers_simple <- ne_layers$major_rivers %>%
  select(any_of("name")) %>%
  st_transform(5880) %>%
  st_simplify(dTolerance = 1000) %>%
  st_transform(4326)

write_geojson(rivers_simple, file.path(data_dir, "rivers.geojson"))

cities_points <- ne_layers$cities_brazil %>%
  transmute(name = NAME) %>%
  st_transform(4326)

write_geojson(cities_points, file.path(data_dir, "cities.geojson"))

rm(write_geojson, brazil, brazil_proj, brazil_simple, biome_names, biomes_simple, resolution_m,
   ne_layers, rivers_simple, cities_points)

```

# 3. Reference sequences

For each primer, the reference sequences of Brazilian species (matched through the synonym list, as in Part 2), with their GenBank accession and whether the sequence is shared with another Brazilian species (ambiguous).

```{r}

# Name (accepted name or synonym) -> accepted name; synonyms shared by several
# species are left out, as in Part 2

syn_table <- stack(brz_mam_synonyms)
syn_table <- syn_table[!syn_table$values %in% syn_table$values[duplicated(syn_table$values)], ]
to_accepted <- setNames(as.character(syn_table$ind), syn_table$values)

sequence_summary <- list()

for (primer in names(brz_mam_eDNA)) {

  db <- brz_mam_eDNA[[primer]]

  seqs <- tibble(
    accession = str_extract(map_chr(db, ~ attr(.x, "name")), "^[^;]+"),
    name      = names(db),
    sequence  = toupper(map_chr(db, ~ .x[1]))
  ) %>%
    mutate(binomial = unname(to_accepted[name])) %>%
    filter(!is.na(binomial)) %>%
    distinct(accession, binomial, sequence) %>%
    group_by(sequence) %>%
    mutate(ambiguous = as.integer(n_distinct(binomial) > 1)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    arrange(binomial, accession)

  rows <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(seqs)), function(i) {
    list(seqs$accession[i], unname(species_id[[seqs$binomial[i]]]), seqs$sequence[i], seqs$ambiguous[i])
  })

  writeLines(
    jsonlite::toJSON(list(primer = unbox(primer), rows = rows), auto_unbox = TRUE),
    file.path(data_dir, "sequences", paste0(primer, ".json")),
    useBytes = TRUE
  )

  sequence_summary[[primer]] <- data.frame(primer = primer, n_sequences = nrow(seqs),
                                           n_species = n_distinct(seqs$binomial))
}

bind_rows(sequence_summary)

rm(syn_table, to_accepted, primer, db, seqs, rows, sequence_summary)

```
